summary: feat(sync): make the default run incremental from a per-(company, resource) watermark (issue #22)
reason: A plain `fiken-cli sync` was a full re-pull of every page of every resource for every company, roughly 1500 sequential requests behind Fiken's one-request-per-token lock, and issue #13 only half-fixed it: the mapping that sends lastModifiedGe landed, but the only thing that ever set a window was a caller-supplied --since. The automatic path was inert because the walker that owns every filtered resource could not use the watermark that existed. sync_state.last_synced_at is read in exactly one place, syncResource, which walks flat resources — `companies` is the only one and it declares no date filter — while syncDependentResource, which walks contacts, journal_entries, transactions, products, sales, invoices and credit_notes, never read it. AND IT COULD NOT HAVE: sync_state is keyed by resource_type alone, so a `sync --company A` run would move a number company B's next pull reads, and B's changes in that gap would never be fetched again. A watermark that can be wrong in that direction is worse than none. THE TABLE is therefore new and keyed on both: sync_watermark(company_slug, resource_type, last_synced_at TEXT, PRIMARY KEY(company_slug, resource_type)), created from migrateExtras — the sanctioned hand-authored migration hook — so a reprint cannot drop it, with the accessors in the hand-authored internal/store/sync_watermark.go. sync_state is untouched: doctor, the provenance envelope, the resume cursor and result_count all still read exactly what they read before, and no schema-version bump was needed because migrateExtras runs idempotently on every open. THE POLICY lives in the hand-authored internal/cli/sync_watermark.go and the generated walker only calls into it. It applies on the DEFAULT path alone (no --full, no --since) and only where syncSinceParamFor answers a parameter; a resource with no temporal filter keeps pulling in full SILENTLY, with no resource_not_incremental warning, because that branch exists to tell a user their --since was dropped and on the default path nobody asked. The value goes through syncSinceWindowValue, so the watermark gets the same day-floor-minus-one treatment as --since (sync_since.go holds the reasoning). READ PER PARENT, not per resource: the window is looked up inside the parent loop from (parentID, dep.Name), because that is the key, and so `--company A` cannot window B. A pair with no row gets no window and is pulled in full — that is a first run, and it is also what a store error degrades to. WRITTEN AS THE RUN'S START, not its end: rows keep changing while a walk runs and an end-stamp would silently exclude everything modified during it. The instant is taken once in RunE into the package-level syncRunStartedAt (the same shape as syncCompanyScope; widening three generated walker signatures to thread one timestamp would buy nothing), with the walk's own start as the fallback for direct calls. WRITTEN ONLY OVER A PULL THE RUN CAN VOUCH FOR: no transport or access error for that parent (parentFailed, which also covers the 403-before-first-page case that the result-count arithmetic deliberately does NOT count as truncation), no truncation (--max-pages cap, stuck cursor, upsert failure, unreadable body, non-JSON 200), and — where Fiken-Api-Result-Count was present — no result_count_mismatch. Anything less leaves the old mark standing and costs one more full pull; advancing past rows nobody fetched loses them permanently. --since never reads or writes it (a caller window is not evidence about what has been pulled), and the user's own --param / --resource-param filters block the write too, via syncPullIsWindowed. --full ignores it, CLEARS the rows of every pair in its scope UP FRONT — in the same breath as clearFullSyncCompanyRows' row delete and before the first request — and writes a new one from the full pull, so an interrupted --full leaves "pull me in full" rather than a mark for rows it cleared and never refetched. The per-parent clear that used to be the ONLY clear stayed on as a backstop for a parent row that appears during the run (this run's own companies pull can add one), and it now reports a failed DELETE as a watermark_clear_failed sync_warning and blocks that pair's advance instead of dropping the error on the floor: a mark the run could not reset is not a mark it may overwrite. FIVE REVIEW DEFECTS were closed on this same record: (1) the lazy clear left a stale mark for every pair an interrupted --full never reached, over rows the run had already deleted, so the next default run windowed over the hole permanently; (2) the failed clear was `_ =`; (3) all_items_failed_id_extraction and primary_key_unresolved dropped rows without blocking the advance, which with no Fiken-Api-Result-Count to catch the shortfall marked those rows pulled forever (parentRowsDropped); (4) the missing-cursor exit and the has_more-without-a-cursor break ended a walk without marking it truncated, leaving the advance's correctness resting on determinePaginationDefaults returning a page-int cursor type; (5) syncRunStartedAt was set in RunE and never reset, so a later walker call in the same process stamped a mark from a run that had ended. KNOCK-ON, deliberate and documented: windowedness is now a per-parent property, so syncPruneDeletedRows takes the parent's window (a watermarked pull can no more conclude a deletion than a --since pull can) and shouldRecordResultCount is told the run was windowed if ANY parent was. The practical consequence is that issue #17's deletion detection now runs on the first complete pull of a pair and on `sync --full`, NOT on the cheap daily run; the existing deletion tests that seeded with one sync and asserted on the next now clear the watermark in between (unwindowNextPull) and say why. VISIBILITY: each windowed pair emits {"event":"sync_window","company":..,"resource":..,"since":..} before its first request, and human mode prints the same fact, because "contacts: 3 synced (done)" beside a company with 900 contacts otherwise reads as data loss. OUT OF SCOPE: doctor shows no watermark column, the flat walker is unchanged, and there is no flag to reset one pair (--full --company X --resources Y already does it).

validated_outcome: make check green (go vet ./..., go test ./..., scripts/check-boundaries.sh). Hand-authored tests in internal/cli/sync_watermark_test.go on a new company-aware fake server (companyServer: per-company rows, per-company 500s, per-company Fiken-Api-Result-Count), because the point of the change is that two companies hold two independent watermarks: FirstRunIsFullAndLeavesAWatermark (no date parameter on the wire, no sync_window event, an RFC3339 UTC mark inside the run's window afterwards); SecondRunSendsTheWatermark (lastModifiedGe equals the mark's day minus one on every request, exactly one sync_window event naming company/resource/since, and no result_count recorded from a windowed pull); CompanyScopeLeavesOtherCompaniesAlone (--company alpha sends zero requests to beta and leaves beta's mark byte-identical while alpha's moves); FailedPairKeepsItsWatermark (beta 500s, keeps its old mark and emits sync_error; alpha's completes and moves); ShortPullKeepsItsWatermark (claimed 3, served 2: one result_count_mismatch and NO mark recorded); FullResetsTheWatermark (--full sends no date parameter, emits no sync_window, replaces testco's mark, and leaves failco — whose --full pull 500ed — with NO mark at all rather than the stale one); SinceDoesNotTouchTheWatermark (the caller's window goes on the wire and the stored mark is unchanged); UnmappedResourceNeitherWindowsNorRecords (accounts pulls in full, records nothing, and does NOT warn resource_not_incremental on the default path); TestSyncWatermarkStore_KeyedByCompanyAndResource (four independent pairs, unknown pair reads "", clear is scoped, an unscoped write is refused); and TestSync_DefaultRunWindowsTheSecondPass, which drives the real `sync` command twice against a live httptest server and asserts the first pass is full, the second carries lastModifiedGe and one sync_window, and both rows survive. Each was checked red against the pre-fix code by disabling the window read, the advance guard and the --full clear in turn. The existing deletion tests (sync_deletes_test.go, sync_empty_body_deletes_test.go) were updated to clear the watermark their seeding pull leaves behind, which is the honest statement of the new behaviour: a windowed pull never deletes, so deletion detection belongs to the first complete pull of a pair and to --full. No live API call was made and no fiken write command was run. REVIEW FOLLOW-UP (same record, five defects): four more hand-authored tests, each checked red against the pre-fix code by reverting exactly its own fix. TestSync_FullClearsWatermarksItNeverGetsToRefetch drives the real command twice — a healthy default run fills contacts rows and a watermark for testco, then the parent table is emptied and /companies answers 404, so `--full --company testco --resources companies,contacts` deletes the contacts rows up front and the dependent walker returns before it ever reaches its per-parent clear; the pair must end with no rows AND no watermark, while a second company's mark is left byte-identical. TestSyncDependentResource_FailedFullClearBlocksTheAdvance installs a BEFORE DELETE trigger on sync_watermark through a second connection (the store's clear has no seam, and dropping the table would break the write too and prove nothing), so --full's clear fails: exactly one watermark_clear_failed sync_warning naming the pair, and the OLD mark still standing afterwards rather than a fresh one. TestSyncDependentResource_DroppedRowsKeepTheWatermarkPut serves a page of scalars with no Fiken-Api-Result-Count header: all_items_failed_id_extraction is emitted, nothing catches the shortfall, and no watermark is recorded. TestSync_RunStartIsScopedToTheRun asserts syncRunStartedAt is back to zero after the command returns. The two pagination exits of defect (4) are defensive: with determinePaginationDefaults' page-int cursor type the page fallback fills nextCursor first, so neither branch is reachable from a test without changing generated pagination behaviour; they are marked truncated so the watermark's correctness stops depending on that.
